response.final_text:
**Proposed disposition:** CLOSE_FP. Confidence is 0.85. The proposal is on file as case C-A-261102-0002, awaiting a human decision.

**Facts that drove it:**
1. All 70 orders are PEGGED children of two parents (P-T-X1102-02-B and P-T-X1102-02-S). Both sides are re-pegged together at the touch, and cancel_symmetry is 0.996. That supports algorithmic re-pricing.
2. There was no benefit from the opposite-side trades. price_move_ticks is 0.0 and reversion_ticks is 0.0. Resting size is 0.87 times depth and distance from the touch is 0 ticks. There was no repetition of the cycle in the session. The 2-tick round trip comes from two-sided quoting.
3. There was no public event (market_wide_cancels_1s_before_first_cancel is 0) and no risk event. The trader has no prior alerts. The 2071 order size is the trader's typical size. The high order-to-trade ratio (46.7) comes from the continuous re-pegging.

**What would change my mind:** evidence that the parents are not a genuine execution algorithm. A one-sided build-up that moved the touch in the trader's favour before the fills would also change it, as would the same pattern repeating in other sessions.

The prior ALGO-EXEC closures in memory are for a different trader on SYN.A. I treated them as context only and checked that the same explanation holds on today's tape.
